headline: Norway Turns Public Toilets Into Destinations
lede: Along Norway’s scenic routes, the humble rest stop gets an architectural second life. Solar-powered facilities frame fjords, weather the elements, and make infrastructure part of the journey.

headline: HackerTube Builds A Calmer Video Feed
lede: A personal index gathers 6,454 videos recommended across nearly two decades of Hacker News comments. Its local recommendations offer an alternative to engagement-driven browsing, assembled with AI assistance but shaped by a human community.

headline: A Pacific Nation Makes Cash Universal
lede: A small Pacific country is testing unconditional payments for every resident. At $800 a year, the program is less a finished social contract than a compact experiment in what basic income can mean at national scale.

headline: A Forgotten Wheat Returns From The Attic
lede: In the 1990s, Claudio Grossi planted seeds saved by his grandfather and found a nearly forgotten Italian wheat. Its revival preserves more than flavor: it restores crop diversity for farms facing drought, poor soils, and a changing climate.

headline: AI Makes Framework Tradeoffs Measurable
lede: A benchmark puts twelve JavaScript frameworks through the same small application, tracking tokens, time, code size, and performance. The results favor lighter server-rendered approaches, while the narrow test leaves plenty of room for judgment.
pullquote: When agents write the code, framework economics become visible.

headline: Hidden Prompts Earn Lawyers A Fine
lede: Two Brazilian law firms hid instructions in white-on-white text inside a court filing, hoping an AI reviewer would skim past its claims. The court treated the maneuver as bad-faith interference and imposed roughly $16,000 in sanctions.

headline: Twenty Years Of Making Files Behave
lede: Two brothers built Zamzar from a focused utility into a durable independent service, converting everything from obscure legacy formats to modern media. The anniversary is a quiet lesson in persistence: solve one recurring problem, then keep showing up.

headline: Critical TCP Flaw Puts Kernels At Risk
lede: CVE-2026-98432 is a Linux IPv4 TCP use-after-free with a CVSS score of 9.8. Patch supported kernels and reboot; until distribution fixes arrive, disable multipath TCP or filter vulnerable traffic where possible.

headline: Five Small Models Solve Harder Together
lede: Memdoor divides programming work among planner, ideator, solver, reviewer, and repair agents connected by files and tests. Across ten LiveCodeBench Hard problems, the workflow scored 9.8 out of 10—an intriguing result, not yet a broad verdict.

headline: Unicode Domains Make Strange Addresses
lede: Internationalized domain names can turn familiar-looking characters into unfamiliar, encoded addresses. The trick is clever—and a reminder that visual similarity in a URL can be a compatibility nuisance or a phishing vector.
